correctness.rationale: PASS: The synchronous Rule 110 constraint for a T-periodic time-column triple (a,b,c) produces a finite directed de Bruijn transfer graph whose rooted spatial n-walks biject with configurations fixed by F_n^T. An independent implementation regenerated 4097 edges at T=6, recurrent SCCs with internal (size,edges) (1,1),(4,4),(9,9), and verified each nontrivial column in these cyclic components has temporal period 2 or 3, excluding primitive temporal six. At T=7 it independently regenerated 16385 edges and two cyclic SCCs (1,1),(63,84). The latter 63-vertex adjacency A yields primitive seven-cycle orbit count tr(A^n)/7 because F_n has one temporal fixed state and 7 is prime. Boolean recurrence on all 63 vertices reproduces exactly the 13 allowed lengths up to 30, while common vertex 193 has 9 and all 31..39 return lengths; concatenating the 9-return gives every n>=31, not a finite extrapolation. Integer trace sample checks n=9,11,14,17,18,20 agree with reported 9,11,2,17,9,60. Direct C++ verification for n<=20 is corroborative only.
